I never expect to lose against Chokepoint, but I enjoy the experience of playing her. This match was the second closest I've come to a defeat in recent memory, with Termination taking her on in Silver Gulch. 

In the final round Unity was incapped, Bunker had one HP, and Absolute Zero was sitting at six with Violent Shivers in effect (no matter what he was going to incap next round thanks to double explosive wagons.) On Unity's turn Bunker managed to put Turret Mode into play and squeeze off a shot with his Explosive Launcher leaving Chokepoint with one hp. My best hope was for the environment to take her out, and there were plenty of options to do so, one unstable portal later Bunker and Absolute Zero are helping Unity back to the present. 

I know a lot of people get down on Chokepoint for not being deadly, and I do wish she were more of a challenge, but I like how she forces you to make due with limited set-ups (especially on Advanced.) This game was an excellent example of that where AZ never kept both modules for long, Bunker started starving for cards, and Unity never had more than two golems out at a time, but they were still effective and felt like they were fighting on despite immense setbacks. Whenever Bunker lost his Flak Cannon he resorted to his Grenade Launcher. All the raptor bots gone? Find a way to destory that Bee Bot and we can keep moving. It felt like improvisational fighting at its best.

After Apostate's failure with Omnitron he thought he might go more traditional dark and creepy and therefore invaded Madame Mittermier's Carnival (CFF, etc.) Luckily a stalwart team of Best of Times Chrono, Prime Wardens Tempest, Ra: Setting Sun, Fugue State Parse, and Adamant Sentinels were there to oppose him. 

This was one of my more interesting fights with Apostate (and I tend to fight Apostate a lot, he's challenging but easy on destruction,) the first round saw Hall of Mirrors come into play which changed my strategy up considerably: Parse doesn't want to discard because the Critical Multiplier will backfire, Ra doesn't have his damaging one-shots so he spends turns building up and making people immune to fire damage that never comes, without Sentinel Tactics the Sentinels are left hunkering down and healing for fear the Idealist will turn on them with all of her specific Villain damage. Those few rounds were full of interesting plays that would usually be second-choice decisions for me. 

At 2 HP remaining Apostate plays a Profane Summons in a game that so far only saw Condemnation, The Peripet, and one Gauntlet, not a big deal right? This is why we keep Buffer Overflows around, I'll just discard it, and wait, shoot he had a second Profane Summons under the first!? He is a devious one. 

Because of that this match became one of the handful of times I've seen Apostate flip, but even so he was dead before he got to act again.

This was my first time playing Visionary: Unleashed and I didn't get to see what she could do; she didn't get an ongoing out until the last round. 

I thought I was in for a tough match but External Combustion, Chemical Frenzy, and Psychic Maelstrom in the first four card plays have a tendancy to remove a lot of obstacles. It's really hard keeping track of titles in the video game, at least on the phone.

(Standard advice of "area-of-effect damage" and "don't use heroes that need to set up" apply.)

posts.name: LewdDolphin21
posts.cooked: The Dreamer was bested by Absolute Zero, Bunker, and Captain Cosmic (all base) in Time Cataclysm. posts.name: KateWalker
posts.cooked:
Well, that was crazy. Decided to use the randomizer to select villains for a Vengeance game. Maximizing hero usage gave me Proletariat, La Capitan, Baron Blade, Miss Info and Plague Rat versus the Sentinels, DW Setback, F6 Tempest, GI Bunker and Completionist Guise in Magmaria. That was rough. Idealist couldn't stay in play, Setback couldn't do anything right (thank goodness for Completionist Guise), and we had a terrible time getting rid of the Impulsion Beam, but after Miss Info fell, things started slotting into place. Eventually, La Capitan was flung into darkness, Baron Blade punched himself to death, and Plague Rat ended up taking himself out by letting loose on Writhe. Never a good idea. I'm so glad I don't have to do that again. D:

And then I noticed that game put the Sentinels as one villain short of a hat trick. Also, KNYFE. Who did they need? Spite Agent of Gloom, of course! Sky-Scraper came along in the Freedtom Tower, and it was a long, fairly boring game, but it turns out two dead teammates, allowing for two uses of Block a round, takes care of most of Spite's hits, especially if Writhe is the highest. He was also flung into darkness in the end. :)

posts.name: KateWalker
posts.cooked:
Spent the afternoon listening to a podcast and playing Sentinels. Only half the games were wins, but here's what I've got:

First, the Adamant Sentinels, Naturalist, DW Fixer and Captain Cosmic against Deadline in Freedom Tower. Felt a lot harder than it appeared to be in hindsight.

Next, a surprisingly long game against Grand Warlord Voss. Adamant Sentinels, GI Bunker, DW Fixer and F6 Wraith had a pretty easy time with him, though. Gotta love that Panzer-Buster when Voss has all his minions out. :D

Lastly, the Infinitor game was a wash (went from "doing okay" to "dead" in the span of one environment turn), but Heroic Infinitor got helped out by F6 Wraith, Omnitron-U, Guise and Setback in the Time Cataclysm.

And I think that finishes those guys off for video game heroes, at least

posts.name: KateWalker
posts.cooked:
Played a bunch of Vengeance this morning. A really rough game against Biomancer, Bugbear, Greazer, Plague Rat and Sergeant Steel nearly ended in a loss for DW Nightmist, Tachyon, Visionary, EoW Bunker and F5 Wraith. It ended up with Nightmist in mist form, watching Plague Rat duke it out with the Final Wasteland. He didn't last long. :B

Then a game that was considerably more rough than I was anticipating. Miss Info, the Operative, Hammer & Anvil, Ambuscade and La Capitan versus DW Nightmist (no one uses her), Visionary, Unity, TN Bunker and F5 Wraith in the Enclave of the Endlings. This time, it was Nightmist, Visionary and Unity who went down by the end.

Last, the Vengeful Five versus Captain Cosmic, Xtreme Haka, Fugue State Parse, Visionary Unleashed and TN Unity in Silver Gulch. That one didn't turn out too badly, if only because no one died. The environment really had me on the ropes, though! Baron Blade and Friction are at single digits each!

Also, I finished off Voss, with F5 Wraith. TNAZ, Ra and Tachyon came along to help. It was brutal. :V

posts.name: KateWalker
posts.cooked:
A couple games while listening to the podcast this morning! First, a long, fairly close game against the Dreamer in Freedom Tower, with DW Nightmist, Tachyon and Expatriette. Tachyon went down, but the Projections were cleaned up shortly thereafter.

And then a game to finish off Infinitor's video game column: Legacy, DW Fixer, Bunker and Chrono-Ranger. Turns out, focusing fire on Infinitor and just letting him do his thing can actually work!

posts.name: KateWalker
posts.cooked:
I don't even know what I'm doing anymore.

Finally got a Chairman win. It wasn't easy, but the Adamant Sentinels and TLT pulled it off despite losing PW Tempest and DW Expat.

Next, a ridiculously easy game against Kismet in the Tomb of Anubis. Adamant Sentinels, Best of Times Chrono Ranger, DC Argent Adept, Xtreme Captain Cosmic and TN Unity beat her up enough that she was kill by fire challenge. :B

And then I started finishing off villains! Akash'Bhuta fell in a remarkably short amount of time. DC Argent Adept, Fused Captain Cosmic and America's Greatest Legacy helped turn Chrono-Ranger into a one-man earth spirit blender. It was beautiful.

Next, another ridiculously easy game: Mad Bomber Blade versus Best of Times, TN Bunker, Setting Sun Ra and TN Unity in Pike Industrial. 3 rounds! Crazy.

Next, an easy if somwhat lengthy game against Chokepoint in the Time Cataclysm. Even with extra card plays from the Computer Room, she couldn't beat Xtreme Argent, Xtreme Cosmic, Horus Ra and DW Nightmist! Though it was the first time I had her flip in rather a while...

Lastly, one more easy game, this time, surprisingly, against Citizen Dawn. The hardest part was getting enough citizens in her trash to auto-flip her! (I started with three I didn't mind keeping in play...) Of course, it didn't hurt that I was playing F5 Bunker, F5 AZ, Xtreme Argent, TN Unity and Xtreme Fanatic.

And then I decided that was enough for a day. :B

posts.name: KateWalker
posts.cooked:
I was supposed to be writing today. I didn't do that. I may not be Sentinelsing responsibly. :(

I had some crazy games today, though. A spectacular loss to Iron Legacy where 60% of my team was down at the start of round 2. A fantastic loss to Matriarch where Chrono-Ranger almost died but Immutus came out and saved him from birds for a round, except he couldn't recover enough to actually hurt Matriarch so he died anyway. D: And then a few worth reporting:

Standard easy game against Unstable Kismet in Dokthorath, with DW Nightmist, Young Legacy, Redeemer Fanatic, F6 Wraith and Visionary. Most of the game was messing with the Talisman once it slipped out of Fanatic's grasp, so she could take all the damage and go Wrathful. :D It worked, eventually!

Then, a surprisingly easy fight against La Capitan in the Tomb of Anubis, with KNYFE Rogue Agent, DC Argent, Best of Times Chrono, Fused Captain Cosmic and Bunker. Nothing special, just regular Bunker. :B

Lastly, a very close game against Miss Information in the Time Cataclysm, with Dark AA, Xtreme Captain Cosmic and Xtreme Tempest. The latter two went down, and it was just Argent, struggling to keep some method of dealing damage in play. But it came down to, discard hand, drop three cards from play, going full-bore with Drake's Pipes and Scherzo. Once on his turn, once on Cosmic's, and did you know Xtreme Tempest has some awful incap powers? He made the Computer Room hit everything for 1, though, which took care of her once and for all.

posts.name: KateWalker
posts.cooked: Only had time for one game tonight, but it was a victory against Iron Legacy! Xtreme Fanatic, Xtreme Tempest, PW Haka, DC Argent and Chrono Best of Times took him out in the MDP!

posts.name: KateWalker
posts.cooked:
Few more games this afternoon. First a very long, yet decently easy game against Skinwalker Gloomweaver, mostly thanks to lots of damage prevention on his flip side and F5 Bunker, Completionist Guise, TN Unity, F5 Tachyon and Xtreme Haka.

Next, revenge on the Matriarch! Parse Fugue State, DW Setback, TN Unity, Redeemer Fanatic and Xtreme Haka took her out in the Final Wasteland, despite all the freaking Skunk Apes. D: Parse and Fanatic fell, though.

Lastly, I finished off Omnitron! Completionist Guise brought PW Haka, Sky-Scraper Extremist and Xtreme Captain Cosmic along to help.

posts.name: KateWalker
posts.cooked:
Haha, okay, finally finished my current run of doing stuff. I'm probably gonna end up finishing this spreadsheet myself, because no one else cares/the fact that I have nothing better to do with my time than play Sentinels all day means I have dominated the challenge, likely driving others off of attempting, and that makes me sad. :(

Oh well. OCD triumphs.

First, a surprisingly easy victory over Cosmotron in the Enclave of the Endlings, with Young Legacy, DW Nightmist, Huned Naturalist, Redeemer Fanatic and DW Setback.

Then, an unsurprisingly easy victory over Plague Rat in the Final Wasteland, with Xtreme Haka, Xtreme Tempest, TNAZ, Fugue State Parse and Sky-Scraper Extremist. Absolute Zero spent so long trying to avoid taking loads of damage from Infection that when the time came for him to open up, Plague Rat was down to like 3 HP and died to Cold Snap.

Progeny was not exactly easy, but Chrono-Ranger Best of Times helped Xtreme Fanatic, DW Setback, Setting Sun Ra and TN Bunker take him down in the Celestial Tribunal.

The Spite game didn't go so hot, but the AoG Spite game was considerably easier! I got lucky with the randomizer: F5 Bunker, Xtreme Fanatic, Omnitron-U, F5 Legacy and F5 Absolute Zero. He had enough time to get all his Drugs out and realize how little difference they made before the heroes beat his dumb face in. :D

Then, Wager Master had a short, fast and ultimately futile game against Chrono Best of Times, TNAZ, Setting Sun Ra, F6 Wraith and Sky-Scraper Extremist in the Block. Absolute Zero went down by the end, but having Breaking the Rules out all game made for loads of card-drawing fun!

Lastly, a big Vengeance game: Biomancer, Bugbear, Sergeant Steel, Ambuscade and Greazer (the villains with the most heroes left) versus DW Setback, TN Bunker, Redeemer Fanatic, Completionist Guise and Ra. Guise made all the difference, swapping Ra to "kill everything mode", Setback to "be useful" mode, and Bunker to "be really useful" mode before starting up the Fanatic blender and ending Biomancer in two rounds. Ra went down, unsurprisingly, but after Bugbear fell, things just seemed to fall into place. And the environment worked like a charm! :D

posts.name: KateWalker
posts.cooked:
Only had time for two games while listening to the Letters Page, and the first one didn't go so hot (though still went better than the Spite AoG game I quit this morning...)

Still, Dark Watch Nightmist, Rook City Wraith and Omnitron-U beat Miss Information in the Tomb of Anubis. Nightmist went down in the final round, but that's okay. Omnitron kinda owns Miss Info.

posts.name: KateWalker
posts.cooked:
Rough morning, woke up early due to tornado warning, whole day a wash, played Sentinels, learned you shouldn't fight the Dreamer in Madame Mittermeier's.

Got some stuff done, though! First, a close game of Cosmotron versus Setting Sun Ra, Rook City Wraith, DW Fixer, Fugue State Parse and Visionary Unleashed in the Enclave of the Endlings. Ra went down, but not without doing tons of damage first. I think everyone was in single digits by the end.

Next, a ridiculously easy game against La Capitan in the Celestial Tribunal. Setting Sun Ra brought the Imbued Fire, Best of Times Chrono Ranger brought the bounties, and Xtreme Argent Adept, Xtreme Tempest and Sky-Scraper Extremist helped clean up.

Then a pretty solid game against the Matriarch, won mostly by virtue of Smoke Bombs. And variant swapping. Setting Sun Ra, TN Bunker, Completionist Guise, Xtreme Tempest and Rook City Wraith triumphed in the Realm of Discord.

Had an easy game against Spite! Only 6 rounds! I'll have to add F5 Bunker to my list of heroes who can really wreck him. And Sky-Scraper Extremist can really nerf his DR with Proportionist. Super-Scientific Tachyon was present.

Another game against Unstable Kismet in Megalopolis with F6 Tempest, DW Expatriette, Horus Ra, Xtreme Fanatic and TN Unity. Nothing really special there.

Lastly, a win against Iron Legacy! KNYFE Rogue Agent, Guise, the Adamant Sentinels, the Naturalist and Fused Captain Cosmic had an easier time once he flipped, thanks to lots of Retcons and Crafty Assaults.

posts.name: KateWalker
posts.cooked:
Morning games turned out well. First designed a Vengeance game that would help me lower Biomancer's count while also finishing off a couple heroes, then finished those heroes off! So it was Biomancer, Miss Info, the Operative, Sergeant Steel and Citizens Hammer & Anvil against Sky-Scraper, Omnitron-X, Chrono-Ranger, TNAZ and Greatest Legacy in the Final Wasteland. And it was one of the easiest Vengeance games I've ever played. I guess it goes to show why those heroes (TNAZ aside) have been used so many times!

Then, to finished off Sky-Scraper, she, Omnitron-U, Tachyon, Freedom 6 Unity and DC Argent took down Unstable Kismet in the Realm of Discord. Another easy game.

Lastly, the unexpectedly easy game: Cosmotron versus Scholar of the Infinite, Eternal Haka, F5 Bunker, DC Adept and Chrono Best of Times in the MDP. I mean, I got lucky with things like stopped Cosmotron's damage dealing right before he played Technological SIngularity, but with the sheer amount of mutual out-of-turn card plays that team has, it was ridiculous. :D

posts.name: KateWalker
posts.cooked: Man, I'm liking this "finishing off heroes". These games are turning out to be really fun! Like PW Captain Cosmic, Scholar, SS Tachyon, Hunted Naturalist and Bunker winning against Greazer, Sergeant Steel, Ambuscade, Bugbear and Plague Rat. Captain Cosmic even got a cool turn where he did tons of damage because all his Constructs were destroyed!

posts.name: KateWalker
posts.cooked:
Almost forgot to record my games!

First, finishing Super-Scientific Tachyon off, with her, Horus Ra and Guise against the Dreamer in Freedom Tower. It turned out to be a much easier game than I anticipated, and Tachyon was great for getting extra Projections out for Ra and Guise to deal with.

Next, to finish off Guise now, it was him, DW Fixer, PW Haka and DW Expat against the Matriarch in the Time Cataclysm. I got stupidly lucky (she put all three Darken the Skies in the trash first thing), and it ended up being an easy game, finished with her on her flip side.

Lastly, a second shot at finishing off Nightmist saw her, PW Fanatic, DW Setback, Scholar of the Infinite and Horus Ra taking on the Vengeful Five in the Final Wasteland. It was a pretty easy fight, all things considered, mostly thanks to a first-turn End of Days. Of course, she's also not done yet, she has to beat Spite still. :B Fun.

posts.name: KateWalker
posts.cooked:
Felt like playing a little today. Finished off Nightmist by taking her, DC Argent and F5 Legacy against Spite in the Time Cataclysm. Argent and Legacy proved to be a fantastic combination, and Argent Adept actually ended up doing most of the damage!

Then, two games to finish off F5 Wraith. First, Cosmotron versus Sky-Scraper Extremist, Tachyon, F5 Wraith, DW Expat and TNAZ in the Final Wasteland. It was a pretty solid challenge, but the heroes triumphed and no one died. :)

Lastly, more Spite, this time EWAZ, Scholar of the Infinite, Redeemer Fanatic and F5 Wraith in the Enclave. That was a fast, surprisingly brutal game, and both Wraith and Fanatic were taken out by the end.

posts.name: KateWalker
posts.cooked:
Been a while. :O Took an opportunity to play a little Challenge mode today, and ended up taking out AoG Spite and Skinweaver with Young Legacy, TLT, Scholar and Dark Visionary. Legacy and Tachyon hadn't beaten Spite yet, so that's two hits! :D

(It was a pretty great game, especially when Scholar got triple Mortal Forms going...)

posts.name: KateWalker
posts.cooked: Had a very depressing Vengeance loss yesterday, which I have since made up for! :V TLT, Xtreme Argent, PW Fanatic, Santa Guise and PW Haka took down Biomancer, Bugbear, Hammer & Anvil, Sergeant Steel and Plague Rat in the Final Wasteland. Getting Santa Guise to work in Vengeance play, you need someone to give him out-of-turn power uses, because you're not likely to get many presents over the course of the game. But once he got started, there was no stopping this team. :) Grinding it down!

posts.name: KateWalker
posts.cooked: Been focused on other things besides playing, but I have some podcasts to listen to today. I took down Biomancer, Hammer & Anvil, Ambuscade, Bugbear and the Operative with Argent Adept, GI Bunker, the Adamant Sentinels, F5 Legacy and Xtreme Haka. Let me just say, that was a fantastic team, it was a fairly easy victory. Bunker helped take down Biomancer quickly, especially once Bastion came out. Argent Adept started with Inspiring Supertonic, meaning we got two extra card plays a round off Legacy. And Haka spent the entire game just setting up and keeping Idealist alive, which was important, because she got targeted by a whole lot of stuff. But using the AA/Legacy engine to power the Sentinels' ridiculous AoE resulted in massive victory. :D

posts.name: KateWalker
posts.cooked: Had a game tonight with Mom. We used the spreadsheet to set up a fight between Citizen Dawn and Completionist Guise, Xtreme Captain Cosmic, Termi-Nation Bunker and Xtreme Tempest in the Enclave of the Endlings. It was a long, stressful game -- 10 rounds! -- but the heroes prevailed in the end. I played Captain Cosmic like a champ, switching back and forth between his forms with Guise to ensure I was always in the right situation to best help. The Constructs survived That Card, and an Augmented Ally on Tempest meant that, once everything was built back up, the heroes were regaining as much health as the villains lost. It was great. :D

posts.name: KateWalker
posts.cooked:
I've been taking the Termi-Nation through all the villains slowly. So far, only lost two: Chairman, no surprise, and, ironically, Chokepoint. <.< Shoulda brought someone else. But that means the occasional slot filled!

With the help of the Sentinels, Termi-Nation took down La Capitan in the Enclave of the Endlings, in a surprisingly easy game.

Then an unsurprisingly easy game against Deadline, with Hunted Naturalist supporting. Coolant Blast is extra-good when you're fighting someone who regularly does lots of fire damage!

Then came the really crazy game: the Dreamer versus Termi-Nation and no one else, on the Mobile Defense Platform. Things were going poorly: Unity was slowly setting up, but the heroes were taking too much damage. Absolute Zero and Bunker went down in the same round before the Dreamer even flipped, and Unity was left with 1 HP. No way I could win, right?

Well, I won. :D Unity at 1 HP was protected by Stealth Bot at 1 HP, because Dreamer was mostly just doing 1's. The occasional Meteor Storm certainly helped, but bit by bit, I was able to wear the Projections down, mostly by sacrificing bots for Volatile Parts to do its magic. I would have lost the Challenge version (after getting 6 Projections under her, one more bot died, and she got smacked with VP), but hot damn, that was an insane win!

posts.name: KateWalker
posts.cooked:
Had another crazy win tonight against Infinitor. PW Captain Cosmic, Absolute Zero and Unity went down on the same turn, leaving Bunker alone with 1 HP. He got a little healing, played a card, did some last-ditch damage with the Omni-Cannon while shouting a war cry and all that. I'm agonizing, because Infinitor's down to 4 HP going into the environment turn...

And then he comes up on the target selection screen for the Time-Crazed Prisoner. Who is going to deal exactly 4 damage.

Well then. :D Suffice to say it was a very satisfying comeback!

posts.name: KateWalker
posts.cooked:
Finished with Termi-Nation! Found out some interesting things, like they're darned good against the Matriarch, and beating Kaargra with TNAZ is gonna be a hard sell. Also, why do I keep losing to Plague Rat? D:

With Captain Cosmic in tow, they helped out Heroic Infinitor in Siver Gulch. One of the hardest Heroic Infinitor games I've ever had!

Then they beat up the Matriarch in the Block, with Super-Scientific Tachyon assisting.

Next was a win against Progeny (seriously, and not against Plague Rat?) in the Time Cataclysm. KNYFE and Unity went down, so it wasn't exactly clean, but oh boy can AZ dish out the damage if he gets a power usage before his turn.

Then, a Wager Master game where I literally did nothing but double-skip and won. They took the right amount of damage to Win by the Odds on the second villain turn, and then a Meteor Storm came out, and Wagey didn't stand a chance. Guise supervised.

Lastly, a fight against the Vengeful Five, with Legacy and TLT in tow. Felt like it took a while, but it was nice smacking Proletariat for 10 cold in one go. :) I mean, you just never get to hit him all that much. (And that netted a whole 3 wins on the spreadsheet. <.< And most of the rest were Absolute Zero.)

posts.name: KateWalker
posts.cooked:
Been stressed, so I thought I'd relax with a few hours of Sentinels and trying to fill in some heroes. It worked pretty well! First, a stupidly easy game of Greazer, Friction, Plague Rat, Sergeant Steel and the Operative versus DW Fixer, TLT, Adamant Sentinels, F5 Legacy and PW Haka. Legacy made that game work, though really, between a first-turn Grease Gun, Heroic Interception, Ground Pound (and potential Hypersonic Assault, which I never saw), the fight was a complete rout. The villains didn't stand a chance.

Next, a bit more of a challenge as Miss Info, Biomancer, Bugbear, La Capitan and Proletariat went up against Legacy, PW Captain Cosmic, TLT, Scholar of the Infinite and PW Fanatic. A lot more fiddly, but it worked out in the end.

Last Vengeance game was Hammer & Anvil, Fright Train, Plague Rat, Sergeant Steel and the Operative versus Legacy, DW Expat, Fixer, Eternal Haka and Ra. Ra was the MVP, with a first-round Drawn to the Flame ensuring he dealt 4 damage to everything every round.

Next, the easiest Miss Info game ever, starring Legacy, the Adamant Sentinels and Visionary. I just don't know what went right! (Well, it was Lead from the Front + Fortitude + villain only does 1 retaliation damage...)

Then another Miss Info game that was considerably harder, but still ended with Eternal Haka, Ra and Tempest alive and (mostly) well!

Legacy, Fugue State Parse, Rook City Wraith, Xtreme Captain Cosmic and Completionist Guise won to the odds against Wager Master at the end of his second turn. :)

Lastly, Unstable Kismet was taken down by DW Fixer, Ra, Tempest, Rook City Wraith and EWAZ in the Enclave of the Endlings. Got to do a 7-points Scorched Earth at one point! :D

posts.name: KateWalker
posts.cooked:
Spent all day playing Sentinels again for some reason. c.c Got to experience the ignominy of a sudden, swift sentencing of the Earth to destruction, for one! I've never felt so blindsided in this game. I mean, compare to the loss against Iron Legacy: he started with +3 damage, beat down half my team, there was no way I was gonna win. But La Capitan suddenly pulls out a double gut-punch to America's Greatest Legacy, and it's just Game Over, and I'm sitting there like "...What?" Amazing.

Anyway, the victories start with Miss Information being defeated by Sky-Scraper Extremist, EWAZ and Tachyon in Megalopolis. Sky-Scraper wrecked her with just a single Hypercortex Stimulator. One to keep in mind!

Then, DC Argent Adept, PW Captain Cosmic, F6 Tempest, GI Bunker and Sky-Scraper Extremist won a close battle against Kaargra Warfang in Freedom Tower. I'm talking "won by two points". We actually had to beat down Kaargra herself! A hard-won victory.

Next, a somewhat close win against the Matriarch. Horus Ra went down in the last turn, but PW Captain Cosmic, Sky-Scraper Extremist (again!) and PW Tempest managed a crazy win. MDP Sky Deck helped!

Then I pulled off a fun win against the Dreamer with Chrono-Ranger Best of Times, Visionary Unleashed and Xtreme Haka. And no, I didn't save the record of that AoG Spite game where I misused CR's variant power. <.< This one was played right.

Lastly, Heroic Infinitor was helped out by the Xtreme Prime Wardens, because the randomizer rolled four of them and I figured, why not? Of course, they were repayed for their kindness by him playing his entire deck in the first two turns. It was just a game of "buckle the heck up and hold on for dear life"!

posts.name: KateWalker
posts.cooked:
Played a couple more games today. First, Miss Info, Greazer, Plague Rat, La Capitan and Sergeant Steel were taken down ridiculously easily by DW Fixer, Argent Adept, F5 Legacy, Ra and Prime Wardens Fanatic. Can't remember the last time I had a Vengeance game where I just took down one villain after another like that. (Fixer MVP!)

The second win was against La Capitan in the Temple of Zhu Long with Scholar of the Infinite, DW Nightmist, KNYFE Rogue Agent, Unity and Rook City Wraith. I'm starting to appreciate the benefits of milking Mysterious Ceremonies for card draws and plays. :3

posts.name: KateWalker
posts.cooked:
I played two more games just because. One ended in a loss. D: Think I'll need a rematch on that one.

But the other ended with Golem Unity, F5 AZ, F6 Tempest, Naturalist and Young Legacy triumphant over Ambuscade, Biomancer, Bugbear, Plague Rat and Sergeant Steel! Who was actually supposed to be the Operative. Who was in the game I lost. :| And this one wasn't a cakewalk, either, Absolute Zero going down near the end. Still, any game you can walk away from...

posts.name: KateWalker
posts.cooked:
My rematch didn't go so well. I blame Santa Guise. :| So I took my frustrations out on some hard solo villains and, uh, that turned out pretty good! :O

Like I said in another thread, Driving Mantis (and Twist the Ether) was the reason DW Fixer, Tempest and Visionary took AOG Spite down with minimal trouble. He was hitting them for 1's and 2's constantly, and there was pretty much nothing he could do to hurt the heroes more than they hurt him. Tempest is great against Spite!

Next, regular Spite had a really bad time against the Adamant Sentinels, Xtreme Captain Cosmic and Setting Sun Ra thanks to a turn-one Imbued Fire. I barely saved any Victims, he flipped too fast, but it didn't matter!

Then, Miss Information got a taste of why you don't mess with Mr. Fixer in the Tomb of Anubis. F6 Wraith and Santa Guise got to watch him Driving Crowbar all over her face, until she fell into the spikes. And then everyone was like, "Ooh, eesh," and just kind of shuffled awkwardly away.

After that, I had a stupidly easy game against La Capitan in the Enclave of the Endlings. Completionist Guise got the Xtreme Fanatic blender going, and it was smooth sailing all the way through. Visionary Unleashed, Tachyon and Expatriette helped! Though Expatriette kind of got torn apart :(

Lastly, a crazy game of TN Bunker, Xtreme Haka, Xtreme Captain Cosmic, Xtreme Argent Adept and Chrono Best of Times in the Block. The environment kicked more butt than everyone else combined; Char had two titles by the time the game was over! The turning point was Haka's 15-ish favor Rampage/Taiaha turn that got him Indiscriminate. Once Kaargra flipped back, we were set.

posts.name: bolnerap
posts.cooked:
I tried a couple games in the video game this morning before heading out on a road trip. Used the random button for both.

A nemesis match between Dark Watch Expat, Dark Watch Setback, GI Bunker, and Visionary went poorly as the entire team went down thanks to Tyler Hayes and a double-Explosives-Barrel chain. Bunker clearly shouldn't have wiped the board of citizens using External Combustion earlier that round. Dawn was down to 29, I might have won if I'd held off on that for another round.

In my second match, Termi-Nation Unity, Redeemer Fanatic, and Prime Warden Captain Cosmic laid waste to Grand Warlord Voss in Pike Industrial. A couple of early Vat Explosions were a little rough and Unity took forever to set up, but we were able to heavily lean on Fanatic. Undaunted + Energy Bracer stopped a lot of minion damage, then Stealth Bot came out just in time to shut down the Trisolvent Vat. I left that vat out for the rest of the game. Every round, Fanatic regained 4 HP from a Vitality Conduit, got to use base power and Absolution thanks to a Dynamic Siphon, and PWCC healed the constructs back to full with the Crest. So, I got to keep Divine Focus out and was still gaining HP. Unity finally got set up and helped deal some damage late in the match to finish Voss before I got buried by Forced Deployment. 

Unity finished at 11, PWCC at 14, and Fanatic at a robust and un-Fanatic-like 23.

posts.name: KateWalker
posts.cooked:
Tried (and succeeded!) to finish off a few villains today. And a few heroes!

First, a crazy game against Skinweaver the Enclave of the Endlings, with DC Argent, Xtreme Captain Cosmic, Fugue State Parse, Setting Sun Ra and F5 Legacy. That Legacy variant is so good, until you run out of cards. XD

Then a two-round game against Heroic Infinitor with DC Argent, Fused Captain Cosmic, Sky-Scraper Extremist, Visionary Unleashed and Completionist Guise. Infinitor played two of his hit-everything one-shots the first turn, so Visionary Suggested them back on top of his deck. Great victory!

Next, a crazy-easy game against Cosmotron in Megalopolis. Fused Captain Cosmic, F5 Tachyon, F5 Absolute Zero and Completionist Guise were, yes, helped out by F5 Legacy. I was actually able to keep Cosmotron from flipping for the first few turns, then doubled-down on the Hypersonic Assaults and Next Evolution/Lead from the Front!

Lastly, another try to finish off Vengeance Blade that actually worked! Dark Visionary, Xtreme Captain Cosmic, Xtreme Tempest, Young Legacy and Santa Guise took out him alongside Ambsucade, Greazer, Fright Train and Proletariat! The key was getting Guise multiple out-of-turn power uses. I got lucky with a first-turn Dynamic Siphon, then followed it up with an Augmented Ally when it got tired. Guise was opening stacks of 5 gifts after just 2 rounds!

posts.name: KateWalker
posts.cooked:
I finished off Fright Train! Ermine, Sergeant Steel, the Operative and Greazer couldn’t save him from the combined might of Completionist Guise, PW Tempest, KNYFE Rogue Agent, Rook City Wraith and GI Bunker!

The game against Proletariat didn’t go so well, so I decided to finish off DW Nightmist instead. First, she brought the Naturalist, RC Wraith and Omnitron along to take down Spite Agent of Gloom. It was a long, somewhat painless fight, where the heroes weren’t dealing a lot of damage, but Spite was dealing even less. I’ll have to remember to use Smoke Bombs against him more often, since Wraith is usually going to get the most benefit from them.

Then, DW Nightmist, GI Bunker, DW Setback and Dark Visionary played an insane game against the Chairman. It was almost an hour long, mostly thanks to dual Twist the Ethers on the True Form and all 15 environment cards in play in short order. Zhu Long beat down the thugs, resurrected them, and beat them down again, while barely touching the heroes. He straight murdered the Operative, dealing 8 damage a round to her for a while because the heroes were doing pretty poorly in the HP department. Setback and Bunker went down and were resurrected multiple times, until Bunker was finally able to get some plating out, which helped him weather the assault of the poisoners. Visionary spent a lot of time cocooned, dealing 1 damage a round to the Chairman for zero retaliation. Nightmist bided her time and finished things off with an Oblivion on the environment’s turn. The ninjas watched.

posts.name: KateWalker
posts.cooked:
Finished off Rook City Wraith this morning! First, she took Omnitron-U, TN Bunker, Expatriette and Xtreme Fanatic along to take out Plague Rat, La Capitan, Greazer, Ambuscade and Bugbear. Expat and Fanatic went down, but Omnitron was MVP, dealing tons of AoE damage and soaking most of what Glamour threw back at the heroes. (I also finished Omnitron-U off! :O)

The second game was against the Dreamer, with Sky-Scraper Extremist actually not making a mess of things and Freedom Six Bunker knowing when to put out consistent damage and knowing when to heal.

Lastly, I decided to cut my losses with Proletariat and left Unity for another game. Instead, Captain Cosmic, Absolute Zero, Redeemer Fanatic and Setting Sun Ra brought Best of Times Chrono-Ranger with them to take out Proletariat, Ermine, Greazer, Sergeant Steel and the Operative. The Operative is murder on Constructs. :C But Absolute Zero and Ra brought the AoE goodness while Chrono and Cosmic played super-good support. It couldn't have gone any better!

posts.name: KateWalker
posts.cooked:
I played a little this morning! Just more Spite games to knock his numbers down. First, Sky-Scraper Extremist, Completionist Guise, DW Expatriette and Xtreme Haka versus Agent of Gloom. It was a stupidly close game: if Haka hadn't taken Spite out with his power, Spite would have won.

And then a regular Spite game, almost as crazy, with Omnitron-U helping out Xtreme Haka, Completionist Guise and Fugue State Parse. Turns out, Completionist Guise and Haka make a good team against Spite!

posts.name: KateWalker
posts.cooked:
Felt like a little Vengeance action after finishing last night's Sentinels Live stream, so I had DC Argent, Fused Captain Cosmic, Santa Guise, PW Tempest and Horus Ra take on Ermine, La Capitan, Operative, Ambuscade and Friction in the Temple of Zhu Long. First, holy crap, won a Vengeance game with Santa Guise! Number two, Temple may be my new go-to for Vengeance wins. It's great being able to guide the ninjas to attack things, and I magically never saw the True Form. But mostly it was a damage race between Ra and Tempest, fueled by Argent Adept, with Ra probably winning thanks to Imbued Fire and Scorched Earth. Finished off the Operative with a ninja!

And now Ermine is done and Santa Guise just has to beat Unstable Kismet! :O

posts.name: KateWalker
posts.cooked: Took the Chairman out of the running for video game heroes. Greatest Legacy helped PW Captain Cosmic, TNAZ and TN Bunker take him down in Freedom Tower. It could have been worse, but it was still a heck of a fight!

posts.name: KateWalker
posts.cooked:
Word to the wise: Completionist Guise loves Captain Cosmic, especially Requital. First round, you let him get a bunch of Constructs on the board, then switch him to Xtreme and use Requital yourself for at least one good card play. And then it's damage-damage-damage all the time! Seriously, I had him dealing upwards of 15-20 per round, Xtreme Captain Cosmic is insane. :D

So yeah, it was Requital CC day. :B Finished off Citizen Dawn with him, Dark Vis, Fugue State Parse, Greatest Legacy and Completionist Guise because being cheesy is fun. :D

Deadline was taken down with a combination of FCC, CG, DC Argent Adept, FS Parse and Xtreme Tempest. And that was a legit team from the spreadsheet! :B

Last, the Ennead fell to FCC, Legacy, Ra, Tempest and Completionist Guise because, again, cheese. :V

posts.name: KateWalker
posts.cooked:
Had some time to myself today: MORE SENTINELS! Just the usual attempts at clearing villains.

First was a decently easy fight against AOG Spite with Best of Times Chrono, Tachyon, DW Setback and Omnitron-X in the Court of Blood. It was pretty trivial, getting around his drugs, though HP got pretty low toward the end.

Next, I'm reporting an older game because I hadn't realized Xtreme Captain Cosmic was the last slot for Ambuscade and not Fused. It was a fun game, played with physical cards with friends, and I remember it because Ra's first play was Flame Barrier, and I just kept stacking Wounding Buffers on him. Every time something hit him, it was annihilated. XD

Next, Deadline was taken out super-fast by Xtreme Argent, Sky-Scraper Extremist, Parse, Legacy and GI Bunker! He even flipped twice!

Easy games were the hallmark of the day, including the fastest Miss Information game I've ever had. Chrono-Ranger BOT tore her apart! Absolute Zero and Visionary Unleashed helped. :B

I had another fast, easy game with Spite in the Tomb of Anubis, with F5 Tachyon, Visionary Unleashed, TN Unity and Omnitron-X. Omni was there to do what he usually does: stay ahead of the put-back drug. With a single Twist the Ether on Spite (Visionary took the other for the damage boost), he was mostly dealing 1's that were soaked by Stealth Bot. Unity had so many bots out that I quite nearly took him out before he flipped (never done that before!) And when it got to the final turn, it was, "Oh! I have enough Burst cards in the trash to Blitz him to death!" It was almost over before it started.

Last was an actual challenge: Finishing off the Chairman with Fused Captain Cosmic and Dark Conductor Argent. I brought Greatest Legacy along because he's about the only hero I can think of who's actually good against the Chairman, and Completionist Guise because he's got tremendous synergy with both CC and AA. It was a long fight, but careful balancing of HP made sure the Final Wasteland focused on the villains more than the heroes. :) And that's every villain up through Deadline finished!

posts.name: bolnerap
posts.cooked: I took out Chairman on Ultimate for the first time yesterday. My linchpin was PW Haka; he's really, really good at shutting down Chairman between Ground Pound, Rampage, and Savage Mana. I even got good use out of Punish the Weak.

posts.name: Lord Flash Fire
posts.cooked: Playing against Chairman is all too easy if you have a Brain burn in your hand turn 1.

posts.name: KateWalker
posts.cooked:
Got a few rounds in this morning, trying to finish stuff off. First, Captain Cosmic, Tachyon, Freedom Six Unity, Wraith and Sky-Scraper Extremist had an easy time against Miss Info, Bugbear, Plague Rat, the Operative and Proletariat in the Enclave of the Endlings. Stealth Bot was key, and then Bloogo came out to protect her, and it was just kind of a slow rout for the heroes. :V And Proletariat's done!

Next, time to finish off Santa Guise. He, TN AZ, Argent Adept and TN Bunker took on Unstable Kismet in Wagner Mars Base. It was a rough game; Absolute Zero ended up being the only hero left, but he was way able to stay ahead of Kismet's damage, even without Violent Shivers. Also, oddly, Kismet has 4 variants left to be defeated by, but only two heroes!

Lastly, I decided to test the might of Completionist Guise, taking him, Xtreme Captain Cosmic and Dark Conductor Argent Adept against the Dreamer in the Celestial Tribunal. It was the easiest Dreamer game I have ever had. Took a while, but no challenge at all.

posts.name: KateWalker
posts.cooked:
Yesterday, I tried to finish off the Wraith and Sky-Scraper Extremist. It didn't go so well. Today, I played the exact same game, merely switching the environment from Final Wasteland to Enclave of the Endlings, and one of the villains for Plague Rat, and I won handily! The hardest part was keeping Sky-Scraper alive, because Thorathian Monolith is just too good in Vengeance. But PW Argent Adept, F5 Tachyon, Wraith, SSE and TN Absolute Zero won over Ambuscade, Greazer, Bugbear, Plague Rat and Sergeant Steel. Though I need to check and see if I misused the Monolith/Smoke Bombs combo...

EDIT: Yeah, I did, but I think the end result would have just been everyone's HP down in the low teens/high single digits, instead of Sky-Scraper hovering around 2 and everyone else in the high teens and twenties.

posts.name: MindWanderer
posts.cooked: I'm getting back into the swing of this, picking up some of the leftovers I can do in the video game.  Dark Watch Setback, Prime Wardens Tempest, and Golem Unity managed to save the Dreamer in the Temple of Zhu Long.  She's really not bad at all with only 3 heroes, despite all three doing their level best to kill themselves, especially in a generous environment.  Unity's Golems actually got kind of dangerous--I'll have to remember not to play too many of them next time, since they ran out of projections to chew on.  They and The True Form (which came out 3 times!) were the biggest danger the team faced.

posts.name: KateWalker
posts.cooked: I actually played a recordable game with friend! :O Xtreme Argent, Fused Captain Cosmic, Visionary Unleashed and Completionist Guise won against Infinitor in the Temple of Zhu Long. It was one of those games where you feel like nothing is going your way for a long time, then suddenly you win. Guise got a fantastic turn when a ninja broke him out of a Crushing Cage just in time for him to Sell Out. And then he swapped Captain Cosmic and unloaded on Infinitor so another ninja could take him out. :V

posts.name: KateWalker
posts.cooked:
I guess I've played these high-end villains enough that I have beating them down to a science? c.c First, an easy game against Spite AOG with Horus Ra, Fugue State Parse, F5 Tachyon and Omnitron-X. The secret is to let Tachyon build up her trash, then fling a few LSBs at him and Blitz him to death. Because otherwise, he'll retaliate and kill her instead.

Next, an easy game against Miss Information with Setting Sun Ra, Expatriette and F6 Tempest. Expat went down, but even with that, it was an easy win. That always makes me wonder if I played wrong.

Lastly, an easy game against Matriarch with Visionary Unleashed, Absolute Zero, Chrono Best of Times and Fused Captain Cosmic, and I cannot actually take credit for this one. She spent the first four rounds messing around with Horrid Cacophanies and Cohorts and Darken the Skies that did nothing (after I Suggested her mask onto the bottom of her deck in turn 2!), so it was just a matter of setting up and unloading. I got super-lucky with her cards, Chrono's cards (By Any Means right off the bat, followed by barrier-breaking Masadah power) and Captain Cosmic's (setting up Chrono to deal tons of damage per round). A Wrest the Mind caused an Inmate to hit Matriarch for 13 at one point. Chrono finished her off with a single plink. :B Why can't they all go like that?

Under 200 matchups left!

posts.name: MindWanderer
posts.cooked: Somehow KNYFE: Rogue Agent tracked down Miss Information in Silver Gulch and confronted her there with the help of Bunker, Termi-Nation Unity, Dark Watch Setback, and Haka.  Nearly lost Setback due to me not having a good feel for how he works (I've only played him twice now), but otherwise it was pretty easy.  Bunker got double-isolated (who cares), and only then did Miss Information get out a Suspicious Malfunction, when KNYFE pulled out a second Suspicious Malfunction.  Sadly Ground Pound doesn't protect against much of what Miss I. has to throw at you (stupid self-damage), but Stealth Bot does, and Termi-Unity makes it inexhaustible.  The Sheriff, after sitting there waiting for her to show up the whole time, ended up being the one to put her down.

posts.name: KateWalker
posts.cooked: Sat down to finish off some heroes and had a good time! PW Argent Adept, F5 Tachyon, KNYFE Rogue Agent, Redeemer Fanatic and Bunker had no troubles with Ambuscade, Biomancer, Hammer & Anvil, La Capitan and the Operative! The two villains that weren't removed from the game by the environment were nuked by Wrathful Retribution. Maybe if La Capitan hadn't decided to shuffle our trashes into our decks, things would have gone differently... :V

posts.name: Lord Flash Fire
posts.cooked: I'll beat up Kaarga tonight.

posts.name: MindWanderer
posts.cooked:
Played a few games.  First, I tried to fill out some of Kaargra's list with Termi-Nation AZ, Argent Adept, Bunker, Dark Watch Setback, and Termi-Nation Unity.  Utter failure.  Tried about 5 times, just couldn't do it.  Closest I came was when I had the 20 points and a big enough blast built up on TNAZ to finish off Kaargra, except she'd picked up The Unbreakable (as a freebie).  She never managed to incap any of the heroes (mostly thanks to TNU's perpetual Stealth Bot recycling machine), and I got the 20 points nearly every time, but we could never get her off the board.

So, I split the team up.  First, Unity and Setback were replaced by The Sentinels and Greatest Legacy.  First turn double Team Communication, Durasteel Chains, Human Shield, Gung-Ho, Counterpoint Bulwark, yadda yadda, easiest win ever.

Second, Dark Watch Setback returned with F6 Bunker and F6 Unity along with the Sentinels again, and Prime Wardens Fanatic.  Didn't get Human Shield this time, so not as easy as I'd hoped, but still got a nice clean win: I was barely losing at something like 15-13 with 4 gladiators in play.  Fanatic had an End of Days, which would have been an instant 5 points (earning Death-Caller as well as 4 kills), so I just had to finish off Kaarga and earn another point somewhere.  Turned out not to matter: Bunker got to use Grenade Launcher 4 times that round, once with a Hasty Augmentation, so he earned plenty of points almost all by himself.

Next, AoG spite was challenged by team Termi-Nation, with Haka and F6 Tempest.  It's all about getting into a groove with him, and I failed to do so on the first try, with almost no victims coming out.  Second try was good, though: Stealth Bot with TNU is always good for defense, especially with Cleansing Downpour, and then I figured out that Ground Pound and Sub-Zero Atmosphere makes for an infinite loop.  I had just gotten out an even better infinite loop (two Ground Pounds and two Reclaim from the Deeps) but had already won; TNAZ is a damage-dealing machine when he doesn't have to worry about self-defense.

Finally, The Matriarch fell to the Argent Adept, Golem Unity, and F6 AZ, with the help of the Adamant Sentinels.  Standard defensive tactics won the day, as usual (Counterpoint Bulwark, TK Thump, and eventually Stealth Bot), although double Cohorts came out early and more than earned their keep.  Super-slow game in the app, once again leaving me wishing for a "Yes to all remaining prompts" option.  She made a last-ditch effort with the last two cards in her deck, wiping out 8 ongoings in 2 rounds, but with 8 HP left I could still Fling her Into Darkness.

posts.name: MindWanderer
posts.cooked:
Couple more that took me a couple of tries.

First, I tried to finish off the video game options for normal Spite by taking Termi-Nation AZ, Termi-Nation Bunker, Prime Warden Captain Cosmic, Dark Watch Setback, and Prime Warden Tempest.  Big fat nope there--they just don't have enough damage mitigation.  Swapping out Tempest for the Wraith did the trick, though: AZ used his power to deliberately commit suicide and get access to his "reduce all non-cold damage by 1" incap while CC and Wraith collected Energy Bracers and Stun Bolts.  Setback's Mitigate kept some incidental damage from getting through until they achieved total lockdown.

Second, Iron Legacy... fortunately, all he had left was two Unities and two AZ's, so I got to assemble the rest of the team to go with them.  First I tried my usual damage mitigation schtick with the Sentinels, but obviously it's been a while since I fought Legacy because that was a horrible idea.  The second game went excellently, though, with the help of Visionary, Redeemer Fanatic, and the Scholar of the Infinite in the Temple of Zhu Long.  Lots of ongoing removal there, and I got nearly the golden chain of Mysterious Ceremonies (all 3 in 2 rounds).  Unity went down, but with all those bonus draws and plays, they achieved two rounds of lockdown with triple Flesh to Iron and Alchemical Redirection.  My plan had originally been to win with a Wrathful Retribution--that's how I win most of my Fanatic vs. Iron Legacy games--but it just refused to come out, while Know When to Cut Loose was much more accomodating.

Almost done with the video game set!  Just the other Unity and AZ left for Iron Legacy, 2 different Bunkers for Miss Information, 4 heroes for AoG Spite (which I'll likely tackle today or tomorrow), and a few scattered single heroes for the rest.  Hopefully Villains of the Multiverse will come out in the video game in time for us to finish them off before OblivAeon's physical form reaches us.

posts.name: KateWalker
posts.cooked: I'm looking forward to Villains making this whole thing that much easier, except it looks like I've been playing Glamour wrong this whole time, and now I don't wanna fight Ambuscade anymore. D:

posts.name: MindWanderer
posts.cooked:
The last video game heroes to face AoG Spite were... Horus Ra, Golem Unity, Argent Adept, and Freedom Six Bunker?!  Wow... every other one has been leftovers that were really hard to win with.  This one's nearly ideal, just missing one component, which, happily, there was a slot left for.  Visionary filled out the squad, making them doubly near-invincible (Twist the Ether+Flesh of the Sun God on one hand, which I had on turn 1, Stealth Bot+Counterpoint Bulwark on the other).  Upgrade Mode and Inventive Preparation left plenty of extra plays for ongoings to get bounced.  Golem Unity, thanks to Flesh of the Sun God and Imbued Fire, was able to summon all the bots she wanted with impunity.  Only drew one Raptor Bot, but it was dealing 10 damage a round by itself.  It was an absolute slaughter.  Only the environment did a little bit of damage, and everyone finished at 20+ HP.

And Iron Legacy's video game foes are also done: Termi-Nation Unity and F6 AZ were actually really helpful, with AZ wiping out most of the ongoings and Unity's bots dealing the lion's share of the damage.  Hunted Naturalist was, for once, utterly useless, but what made this a cinch was Tachyon starting with a Hypersonic Assault and a Lightspeed Barrage in hand, and another Barrage she played off the bottom of her deck.

posts.name: MindWanderer
posts.cooked:
Man, Kaargra is just the worst.  I went to finish off her last video game hero, Termi-Nation Unity, with her, and since her allies didn't matter I went for overkill with Legacy, SS Tachyon, Omnitron-X, and Scholar.  And at the end of round 2 it was going great--one gladiator left with 1 HP who'd been Assaulted and couldn't deal damage, score was 5-11 in my favor.  Then Kaargra gets Bloodsworn Judgement, Get Back In There, which brings back Idesa the Adroit, who picked up Stonejaw, Fickle Fans, and all of a sudden it's over at 20-7.  It's just not fun when that happens, there was really hardly anything better I could have done.  In retrospect it would have been smarter for me to not kill any gladiators at all so Get Back In There wouldn't grab them (Idesa had been Assaulted, too), but I would have been fine if virtually anything else had happened there.  Ugh.

Rematch went cleanly, though.  Wiped out all the gladiators in round 1 just to make sure Kaargra played only two cards instead of 3, then wiped the floor with her in round 2.  Final score 3-30.

posts.name: Lord Flash Fire
posts.cooked:
Damn it, I forgot to finish Kaarga!

Good on you for filling in, MindWanderer.

I'll' just sit over here and finish Amina

posts.name: Lord Flash Fire
posts.cooked: Beat her up with EoW Bunker, Legacy, Sentinels, Unity, and Mr. Fixer. Easy.

posts.name: KateWalker
posts.cooked:
Alright, jerks, I'm back, let's do this. :V

Made a single attempt this morning, which turned into a ridiculous to-do and a slow, squeaky "there's no way they can win" victory for DC Argent, Fused Captain Cosmic, F5 Absolute Zero, F6 Wraith and the Naturalist over Miss Info, Hammer & Anvil, Greazer, the Operative and Sergeant Steel. It ended with Citizen Hammer and the Operative versus AZ and the Naturalist, who was just untouchable (minus the huge Thermal Shockwave blowback he ate thanks to Indomitable Force). The environment was the only thing that killed heroes: Smoke Bombs plus Naturalist as the highest is an amazing combo. The last turn was Naturalist eating through two Scorching Snaps so he could do a single damage to the Operative and take her out. No waiting for the environment to kill-steal! >:V

posts.name: KateWalker
posts.cooked: One more! Fugue State Parse, Expat, Xtreme Tempest, Haka and Fanatic against Miss Info, Biomancer, Bugbear, Hammer & Anvil and the Operative in the Temple of Zhu Long. None of the heroes fell, but everyone had either 2 or 3 HP by the end. :B Expatriette's done!

posts.name: KateWalker
posts.cooked: Went through one today: Xtreme AA, Completionist Guise, Visionary Unleashed, Xtreme Haka and Setting Sun Ra against Kismet in the Temple of Zhu Long. It didn't feel easy, but given everyone had better than 15 HP by the end, and most heroes had over 20, it was pretty easy. :B

posts.name: KateWalker
posts.cooked:
According to the new posts page, no one's posted here all day (until right the heck now), which made me antsy. D: It's Captain Cosmic time!

First, I finished off the Dreamer with Fused CC, Scholar and Redeemer Fanatic in the Final Wasteland. It was a fairly standard Dreamer game, all things told. (Don't Dismiss Anything into an End of Days kind of sucked, but it could have been worse.)

Then I had a terrible game against Infinitor: 3 rounds, totally smoked the heroes, no way we could win. I then turned around and did the opposite to Kismet: 3 rounds, totally stomped her, no way she could win. Xtreme Fanatic, Xtreme Tempest, Fused CC and a randomized Setback had a field day.

Lastly, I said 'nah' to a bunch of potential matchups and instead took on Plague Rat with Xtreme Fanatic, Fused CC, Setting Sun Ra, DC Argent Adept and Chrono Best of Times in Megalopolis. It was a brutal game. Chrono's last play was Hunter and Hunted, so he was dealing 8's to Plague Rat, but all of a sudden, literally everyone was Infected, and with an Afflicted Frenzy on the board! No one actually died, but I think Chrono would have if not for Ra's super-powered Drawn to the Flame. Whoof.

posts.name: KateWalker
posts.cooked: Tried to get a few games in, and most of them didn't go so hot. The one exception was Absolute Zero and GI Bunker bringing Visionary Unleashed, Xtreme AA and Sky-Scraper along to fight Unstable Kismet in Silver Gulch. Go figure, the round I play Thorathian Monolith is the round Kismet destroys the Explosives Wagon, but at least Sky-Scraper was the only one who went down. It was an intense game, but fairly easy, standard for U Kismet. And hey, now GI Bunker's done. :)

posts.name: KateWalker
posts.cooked:
Comin' at that ol' spreadsheet like a hurricane! >:V First, a Spite game to finish off F5 Absolute Zero. He brought Best of Times Chrono Ranger, Xtreme Tempest and Sky-Scraper Extremist along and, wow, that was a total rout. Between AZ and Chrono, Spite didn't stand a chance, and only had four drugs out when I killed him. :D I finally did it!

Next, to finish off Miss Info, Fugue State Parse took Omnitron-U and DW Fixer to Freedom Tower. It wasn't exactly easy, but they turned out to be a great team.

Next, taking the fight to Plague Rat was Xtreme Captain Cosmic, with Omni-U, Legacy, F6 Wraith and KNYFE RA assisting. Ol' Ratty didn't stand a chance. But then, he wasn't meant to. :B

Then, some Vengeance! Miss Info, Ambuscade, Greazer, La Capitan and the Operative faced F6 Tempest, Bunker, DW Expatriette, the Naturalist and Fanatic in the Temple of Zhu Long. They actually had to bring Fanatic back to life at one point (wanna bet she wasn't happy about that?); otherwise, none of the heroes fell.

Lastly, Hammer & Anvil, Biomancer, Sergeant Steel, Plague Rat and Proletariat (who had no reason to be there!) took out Dark Visionary, F6 Tempest, DW Expatriette and Fanatic... but not Haka. That was a really close game. D:

posts.name: KateWalker
posts.cooked:
Went through a few late-alphabet games. First, a lovely one-round game against Wager Master. DC Argent, Fused Captain Cosmic, Bunker, Xtreme Tempest and Visionary Unleashed did the math to win by the odds!

Next, Agent of Gloom Spite attacked the Block, and Omnitron-X brought DC Argent, Fused Captain Cosmic and Visionary Unleashed to help kick his kiester. Oddly familiar team, that...

Lastly, DC Argent, Xtreme Captain Cosmic (different!), Setting Sun Ra and Visionary Unleashed brought KNYFE along to kick Progeny's butt and OH BOY is the Court of Blood a really great place to fight him. No healing means Scion of Frost is useless, and no radiant damage means he's mostly helpless on his flip side. Great neat secrets discovered!

posts.name: KateWalker
posts.cooked:
Had some fun this morning. First, I finally took out Infinitor with those last five heroes. It was NOT easy. Parse and Argent went down, and in the end, it was "We're gonna lose by 3 HP, oh wait, I can hit Infinitor with the self-damage from Embolden, now we're gonna lose by 1 HP, oh wait he killed himself." Seriously, I'm not sure they would have lasted that final round otherwise.

I cleared Kaargra Warfang with Completionist Guise and Fused Captain Cosmic, alongside Legacy, Fanatic and Tempest. Tempest with Seeker and Living Weapon was the reason the heroes won, given that Kaargra flipped twice. Final score was 14 to 30-something, I kind of lost count.

Next, I pulled out Bunker to take on Trickster Kismet (since that's apparently what she's called now!) And after rolling both vanilla Wraith and vanilla Legacy, I said heck with it and just took the whole Freedom Five along. It was a pretty easy game, no surprise there.

Lastly, I took on La Capitan with DC Argent, Legacy, Xtreme Captain Cosmic, Xtreme Haka and the Wraith in the Tomb of Anubis. It was a pretty standard La Capitan game, all things considered.

Still can't beat Iron Legacy with those last few heroes, though...

No surprise I've been playing a bunch of Vegeance games recently! Not actively trying to fill in the spreadsheet, but picking off bits here and there when I can.

First, well first win anyway, was La Capitan, Proletariat, Baron Blade, Ambuscade and Greazer against Chrono-Ranger, Unity, PW Tempest, F6 Wraith and Sky-Scraper in Silver Gulch. That one was pretty easy, I think.

Next, Greazer, Miss Info, Ambuscade and Hammer & Anvil against PW Captain Cosmic, EWAZ, F6 Unity and TN Bunker in the Final Wasteland. That one I remeber definitely that it ended with Greazer and Ambuscade out of the game, the latter ending it. :D

Then, a bunch of Miss Info fights because I'm going through checking out all the nemesis dialogue. :B First, her, Sergeat Steel and Greazer against Legacy, AZ and Horus Ra in the MDP. Another easy game!

Next, Miss Info, Greazer and Biomancer against Young Legacy, Horus Ra and Nightmist in the Tomb of Anubis. That was a close game! I ended with all heroes standing only because I left all the Trials in play and bounced their damage off Nightmist onto Biomancer. D:

Lastly (man, a lot of these games don't count), Miss Info, Friction, Ermine, Bugbear and La Capitan against Tachyon, Dark Visionary, EOW Bunker, Legacy and AZ in Magmaria. (I rolled Magmaria a lot today...) Absolute Zero ended up dying to Crystalloid Behemoths, but he made a good show of it. Tachyon finished the game with a Sucker Punch!

We're down to the last percentage point!

The first one I set up ti finish off the Operative: her, La Capitan, Miss Info and Proletariat versus Mr. Fixer, PW Captain Cosmic, F6 Bunker and DW Setback in the Final Wasteland. Pretty easy game, all things considered, thanks to Fixer and a few Dynamic Siphons.

The other was Plague Rat, Biomancer, Ambuscade, Ermine and the Operative against Eternal Haka, Scholar of the Infinite, Sky-Scraper, Absolute Zero and Unity in Pike Industrial. Lots of damage. So much damage. Everyone died but Haka, it was kind of amazing.

posts.name: KateWalker
posts.cooked:
Played a couple games today. Tryna finish off them non-game heroes now that all the released villains are (technically) in the video game.

First, a long, dull fight against the Matriarch. DC Argent and Xtreme Captain Cosmic brought Omnitron-X and Scholar along, which is good, because they're the only ones who made it out alive. With Defensive Displacement out for a number of rounds, no one but Omnitron was dealing damage, and though he hit Matriarch a few times with his Plasma Cannons, it all came down to about four or five Grace Under Fires, turning the tide of birds against the big birdy lady.

Next was a Vengeance game that didn't go so well, but the one after that did. Unity, Best of Times Chrono-Ranger, Xtreme Tempest, Setting Sun Ra and Xtreme Haka prevailed against Bugbear, Friction, Hammer & Anvil, Sergeant Steel and Greazer in the Enclave of the Endlings. None of the heroes went down! Haka kept Unity and Chrono alive for a while, Tempest dealt all the damage, and Ra, toward the end, said "Screw it" and unleashed a Solar Flare-powered Blaze of Glory on everyone, including himself.

There are 14 matchups of each type left. DAWN OF THE SECOND DAY

posts.name: KateWalker
posts.cooked:
I've come to the conclusion that it was going to take more than one game to finish this thing off. I was right.

My go-to Iron legacy-killing team is Fugue State Parse, Chrono-Ranger and Haka, and I just so happened to roll Freedom Tower, so I played all three games there.

The first, with Xtreme Captain Cosmic, went swimmingly. It was a textbook Chrono-Ranger victory over Iron Legs. The only thing that went wrong was Captain Cosmic pulling too much damage off a Harsh Offense and hitting Haka. But it didn't matter.

The Setting Sun Ra game didn't go so well. :C

The Visionary Unleashed game fared little better, but Parse was able to stand alone and finish him off with the help of her friends. Mission Control leaves an Impossible Shot on top, Haka and Visionary die on Legacy's turn, and then it's Quick Calc to put Impossible Shot on the bottom, play it with her power, induce Legacy to hurt himself with Visionary's incap, and play another Impossible Shot off Chrono-Ranger's. Just enough damage.

So we're down to one matchup.

Who will defeat Iron legacy with Setting Sun Ra to claim ultimate glory?

Or at least a little glory.

I hope it's someone else. :B
